blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.subject: Princes’ Burial Chamber tier
blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.observation: The gallery index labels the chamber Tier 4 while a later caption on the same gallery calls it Tier 1; the existing archive also places it on Tier 1.
blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.decision: Preserve the chamber as a confirmed visual record but set tier to unresolved-tier. No tier anchor or traversal route may be authored until chapter-level evidence resolves the conflict.

blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.subject: Room 3125 versus Room 3101
blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.observation: Hunterpedia records that the weekly Chapter 410 text used Room 3125 while the author correction identifies the intended room as 3101.
blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.decision: Use Room 3101 as the canonical scene identity. Keep 3125 only as a non-navigable legacy search alias with an explicit correction note.

blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.subject: Heil-Ly official office versus concealed operational base
blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.observation: The registered Tier 3 office and the concealed base between Tiers 2 and 3 are distinct locations that can be collapsed by casual naming.
blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.decision: Maintain separate canonical IDs, labels, evidence, and route records. Never use office imagery as geometry for the secret base or vice versa.

blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.subject: Tier 1 plan north versus ship bow
blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.observation: The article describes room rows using an assumed north relative to the banquet hall, but does not equate diagram north with the Black Whale bow.
blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.decision: Use local plan coordinates only. Do not rotate the plan onto +Z bow until an independent exterior/plan relationship is found.

blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.subject: Cross-section tier dimensions
blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.observation: The canonical cutaway confirms tier order and broad envelope but supplies no metric grid for individual tier heights or interior positions.
blackWhale3dReferenceIssues.decision: Use it for stacking and envelope ratios only. Do not derive exact deck heights, room coordinates, or passage widths from pixels.

blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.label: Royal monumental thresholds
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.description: Tier 1 uses tall symmetrical gates, long ceremonial axes, paneled walls, and unusually large ceiling volumes.
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.allowedUse: Guide a shared Tier 1 design language without cloning one room into another.

blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.label: Ornate royal interiors
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.description: Patterned floors, framed art, decorative ceilings, and formal furniture distinguish royal and VVIP space.
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.allowedUse: Material and furnishing vocabulary only; not evidence of identical layouts.

blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.label: Institutional ceiling and wall grids
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.description: Justice, police, army, court, and safety spaces repeatedly use rectilinear bays, panel grids, and controlled sightlines.
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.allowedUse: Shared kit-of-parts only after each room keeps its own confirmed proportions.

blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.label: Dense public concourses
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.description: Lower-tier public spaces combine high occupancy, large signs, open floor areas, and visible service ceilings.
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.allowedUse: Crowd and circulation atmosphere; not a floor-plan generator.

blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.label: Industrial service framing
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.description: Bulkheads, warehouses, assembly points, and launch spaces use exposed rails, wide clearances, repeating structural frames, and utility surfaces.
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.allowedUse: Service-space kit reference with source-specific geometry retained.

blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.label: Repeating detention modules
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.description: Cells and corridors use compact rectilinear rooms, repeated doors, plain wall panels, and controlled thresholds.
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.allowedUse: Modular visual language; individual cell identity and dimensions remain source-bound.

blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.label: Heil-Ly bunker domesticity
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.description: The concealed base mixes plain reinforced rooms with domestic furniture, communal utilities, and abrupt controlled doorways.
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.allowedUse: Internal base mood and function; no inferred adjacency.

blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.label: Panoramic glazing and curved envelope
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.description: Observation and vehicle spaces use curved shells and broad view apertures that contrast with rectilinear interior modules.

blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.label: Oversized location signage
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.description: Lower-tier wayfinding uses large numeric or venue markers visible above crowds.
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.allowedUse: Wayfinding style; exact numbering remains chapter-specific.

blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.label: Rectilinear city inside an organic hull
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.description: The whale-shaped exterior encloses stacked, predominantly rectilinear civic, residential, and industrial volumes.
blackWhale3dArchitecturalMotifs.allowedUse: Macro art direction, not permission to fill unknown space.
